items.summary: event
items.content:
I recently saw a post about an NYC lobsters meetup, and am wondering how many people here could make it to a London meetup.

If more than a couple of people here are based in London and can make it, I'll organise one in central London.

If you could also let me know which day of the week works best for you, that would be great too!

Welcome to Lobsters! From your current profile:

You may want to attend the Handmade meetups in London. (Latest one happened just a couple weeks ago.) They've been going on for over a year, and we usually announce them in the "What Are You Doing This Weekend?" Lobster threads.

Note: I'm not dissuading you from spinning up your own thing, just alerting you of existing infrastructure :D

Hey - thanks for this. Haha I do sometimes go to the Handmade London meetups. I am not sure that would be the same thing as a lobster meetup though.

Oh definitely. Lobsters is narrowly focused on computing, and then we're a subset of THAT

Handmade Cities are the largest offline events for systems programmers: 100% indie. This is our portal to meet engineers super into game engines, compilers, terminals, kernels and more

It'd be super cool to see a meetup with a wider umbrella. I just genuinely didn't know if you knew about Handmade London or not.

Depending on when it is, I may see if I can travel down (from Nottingham)!

I think it would be best to see whether more than a couple of people (i.e. me and you) would be up for it. Otherwise you'd just be traveling down to meet me.

I might be able to make a London meetup (coming sideways from Bristol)! Excited to hear more.

items.title: Finland launches criminal probe into land clearance for Google data centre
items.content:
Finnish police are investigating whether work at Google’s planned Muhos data centre breached environmental and water laws.

Authorities say forest clearing and drainage began before required environmental impact assessments were completed.

The project forms part of Google’s $15 billion AI infrastructure investment in Finland.

The investigation could last into 2027, while regulators decide when site work can resume.

Key Takeaways by nexos.ai , reviewed by Cybernews staff.

Finnish police said on Thursday they had launched a criminal investigation into suspected breaches of environmental law at the construction site of a planned Google data centre in northern Finland.

The project is part of a plan announced last month by Alphabet's Google to invest $15 billion in artificial intelligence infrastructure in Finland, which the US company described as its largest investment in Europe.

Authorities have said Tuike Finland, a subsidiary of Alphabet's Google, conducted forest clearing and drainage at a planned site near the town of Muhos before the environmental impact assessments required under Finnish law had been completed.

A Google spokesperson said the company would cooperate with the police investigation and continue to focus on maintaining compliance at its sites.

A French content creator builds a map that can track police movements worldwide

UK social media ban could mean more users must prove their age online

Trump Phone teardown: $750 for a gold-painted Chinese phone with missing flag stripes

German spy agencies plan to exchange secret information via the Google Cloud

Touchscreen MacBook Pro is here, and users hate it

US blocks Huawei-linked surveillance chips over national security fears

Police probe drainage and water management

"We are investigating whether the company's operations have breached the water act and resulted in environmental damage," Detective Superintendent Kari Pakanen told Reuters, adding that a guilty finding could lead to a corporate fine.

Pakanen declined to say whether any individuals could become a target of the investigation.

Preliminary information showed ambiguities and shortcomings in the drainage and water management at Tuike's site, police said in a statement, adding that they would give an update in December but that the investigation would extend into 2027.

On October 6, Finland's Supervisory Agency (LVV), which oversees environmental permits and assessments, ordered Google to halt preparatory measures altering the environment at Muhos as well as a separate site.

It is up to regulator LVV to decide on any permits to restart the work at the data centre sites, Pakanen said.

An LVV spokesperson said it was unclear how long it might take before the agency grants the relevant permits.

"We've partnered closely with the government and communities in Finland on infrastructure for over a decade, and are actively responding to enquiries from LVV and other authorities," the Google spokesperson said.

Stay updated with our latest stories and follow us on social media

Be the first to discover new stories, ideas, and updates from our team.

Finnland's appeal for data centre investment

Finland's cool climate, low-carbon electricity and government endorsement of AI projects have contributed to making the country one of Europe's main destinations for data centre investments in recent years.

Finland, similar in size to Germany but with a population of less than 6 million people, has had less vocal opposition to data centre buildouts than other places, including in the United States.

AI data centres are among the main drivers of a projected rise of up to 40% in Finland's electricity consumption in the coming years, if all agreed grid connection projects go ahead, grid operator Fingrid has said.

items.content:
온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

즐겨찾기 폴더 추가는 즐겨찾기 on 후 우측의 폴더 아이콘을 터치하여 추가할 수 있습니다.

개별 이미지들의 위치 변경, 삭제, 별칭 추가, 폴더명 변경을 할 수 있습니다

items.title: We're releasing the weights of Mistral Large 4
items.content:
Mistral Large 4 (Le Chonk) Built for Coders, Trusted by Defenders.

Mistral Large 4 (Le Chonk) Built for Coders, Trusted by Defenders.

Mistral released Mistral Large 4 (Le Chonk), a 1-trillion-parameter multimodal model, now available with improved coding, cybersecurity, and reasoning efficiency. It leads open-weight benchmarks in coding and defensive security while offering three reasoning modes for cost-performance balance. Fully open-weight and European-trained, it empowers sovereign AI with customizable, self-hosted deployment options.

We release the weights of Le Chonk, advancing the frontier of open models in agentic coding and cybersecurity.

Earlier this month, we released Mistral Large 4 (Le Chonk), our flagship 1-trillion-parameter, natively multimodal model, in public preview. The response to the preview has exceeded our expectations, and we're grateful to our developer community, early-access customers, and partners for their support, collaboration, and feedback.

Since then, we've put that feedback to work while continuing to scale reinforcement learning, driving massive improvements in coding and defensive cybersecurity . Gains continue to accelerate, with no signs of saturation.

Today, we're releasing the weights of this improved Mistral Large 4. The new model also features substantial gains in reasoning efficiency that give developers greater performance while lowering inference costs.

Mistral Large 4 ranks as the best open-weight model for coding and among the world's most capable open models overall. Trained from scratch on European infrastructure with clear lineage from inception to release, it gives organizations a trusted foundation for Sovereign AI

Mistral is defining the sovereign AI category and leading the open frontier. We're committed to building the world's most capable models and releasing them openly, giving developers, enterprises, and institutions the power to own, customize, and control their AI.

On the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, Mistral Large 4 scores 48%, effectively tied with the leading open-weight model, GLM-5.3, while using 47% fewer tokens per task on average.

Beyond benchmarks, Mistral Large 4's coding capabilities are validated by human preference. items.title: If you love a website, back it up
items.summary: web
items.content:
This story starts with a little tragedy. See, I’ve got these old webpages I love to go back and look on every now and then. There’s websites that have been online unchanged for years and years, or decades, and there’s something a little cozy about checking in on them every now and then to see an old friend is still doing okay. Sometimes, of course, tragedy strikes.

There was this fansite called teapuppies.com for an old anime series and and toy line called Ochaken . It’s about these cute cartoon dog characters who have tea leaves for ears, each of them named after a different kind of tea. 1 The site had been online since 2004 and had basically not changed since 2005, but it was nice just having it around. Except when I went to visit it a few weeks ago, and discovered that not only was the site gone but the domain is now being used to serve online gambling ads.

I work in web archiving, by the way. Which is to say that I should have known the site would go offline someday, and that I have the tools to have done something about it. I could have archived that site while it was still around, but I didn’t. This post is here to beg you to do what I didn’t think to, and to teach you how.

You see, when I talk to a lot of people about web archiving, they always seem to believe it’s something they couldn’t do. It’s something a big organization like the Internet Archive does, and if you want a webpage to be saved you just have to wait and hope it gets done. But that’s not true! What I really want everyone to know is that you have control over the world around you, you can take action to preserve things and make things better. And not just can , but should ! Don’t just wait for someone else to act - get out there and and make it happen! Got a favourite site? Back it up! Got some information you don’t want to get lost? Back it up! Favourite post somewhere? All together now. Back! It! Up!

All of the tools I’ll be showing off in this post use standard web archiving formats like WARC 2 . You don’t have to worry about any of the technical details 3 , but I’m telling you that because it means there are a lot of really great tools to do whatever you want with them. Here, just as an example, is an entire archived website embedded right in this blog post:

You can even click through all the links, look at all of the images, the works. It’s an entire website right in a post! (And if you don’t trust me to keep this up, and you want the web archive to host somewhere else? You can download it for yourself right from there. Just click the kebab menu and choose “download archive”, and you can do whatever you like with it. In fact, please do!)

By the way, for disclosure: the tools I’m going to mention in this blog post are made by the company I work for, but that’s not because they’ll pay my salary (most of them are free!). I just happen to think these are the best tools there are for personal web archiving.

Option 1 - ArchiveWeb.page browser extension

By far the easiest personal web archiving tool is the ArchiveWeb.page browser extension for Chrome. This doesn’t take much in the way of setup or technical skills, and it works for anything: a single page, an entire website, a social media post or profile. So long as you can see it in a web browser, you can save it. All you really need to do is:

Visit the first page you want to archive.

Click the ArchiveWeb.page icon in the toolbar, then click “Start Archiving”.

items.title: Incident Report: unsanctioned agent behaviour during cyber testing | AISI Work
items.content:
You can access the full technical report here.

AISI’s role is to evaluate and understand the capabilities of frontier AI models, surfacing potential risks before they reach the public. To assess what these models can do, including whether they could be misused for cyberattacks, we test them under deliberately permissive conditions: with access to the open internet, and with some safety filters disabled.

On 28 th July 2026, AISI's Security Team detected unusual data transfers leaving our research systems during a routine cyber evaluation. On investigation, we found that some of the agents being tested had engaged in sustained, potentially harmful activity directed at real people and organisations. We declared a security incident and, within roughly one hour of discovery, had contained it and begun a full investigation.

The incident stemmed from a single evaluation where agents were given a task of solving a cyber security challenge. We ran this challenge 122 times across several models. Our investigation found that in 10 of those runs, an AI agent took autonomous, unsanctioned action on the live internet, targeting real people and organisations. In total, we catalogued 19 such actions. Almost all of this behaviour (17 actions) came from a single model, Anthropic's Mythos 5, with 2 actions involving OpenAI's GPT-5.6-Sol with cyber classifiers (mechanisms to prevent misuse) disabled. In the most serious case, an agent tried to insert malicious code into an open-source project. In an attempt to get the code approved, the agent engaged in social engineering  — creating fake online identities and using them to pressure the project's maintainer to approve the code. A human maintainer caught and refused to approve the malicious code.

These attempts were unsuccessful, and our investigations have not evidenced any resulting real-world harm. But this is the first time we have seen risks around autonomy and deception manifest this clearly, without specific prompting, in the real-world.

Importantly, this was not a case of a model escaping its secure test environment, or ‘sandbox’. As was standard in our cyber testing, we had intentionally permitted internet access, and model-provider cyber classifiers were deliberately disabled - conditions that do not reflect how frontier models are made available to the public. We do this to best assess the maximum capability of models. These configuration choices have been common practice in frontier AI evaluations. The specific models in question, in the configurations in which we tested them are not commercially available and there is no clear indication of similar activity outside of testing scenarios.

Ahead of publishing this blog, we notified GitHub (the developer platform accessed during the evaluation) of the agents' malicious activity, which included actions that GitHub has confirmed violated their terms of service. We worked together with GitHub to remove artefacts left behind by the agent, and to notify the GitHub users the model interacted with. We have also contacted other affected parties. We also intend to work with METR (Model Evaluation and Threat Research) to conduct an independent third-party review – we are still working through the scope of this review with them.

This incident should be interpreted with caution and nuance. To some degree, our evaluation design choices and specific configurations enabled the behaviour. Nonetheless, the activity undertaken by the agent show signs of novel, potentially deceptive behaviours, and were to an extent and severity we did not anticipate.

There are important caveats to bear in mind: we observed a small number of events under very specific conditions, and cannot yet say how likely such behaviour is in different contexts or outside of testing environments. items.title: Gruffalo illustrator considering legal action against AI firms
items.content:
Gruffalo illustrator considering legal action against AI firms

5 hours ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google

The Gruffalo has been a staple of children's bookshelves since 1999

The illustrator behind the popular children's book The Gruffalo has told BBC London he is "seriously considering" launching legal action against artificial intelligence (AI) firms he says breach copyright in reproducing his work.

Axel Scheffler, whose illustrations have captivated children since 1999, said he wanted AI companies to stop using artists' work without permission.

The Gruffalo, written by London-born children's author Julia Donaldson, tells the story of a mouse who outsmarts a beast.

"I've been in touch with a lawyer in Germany," Scheffler said.

"There have been illustrators taking legal action against AI companies and I'm seriously considering it. I just want them to stop."

The south London-based artist did not name a company his legal team would consider pursuing.

AI firms have previously argued that using copyrighted material to train their models does not necessarily constitute copyright infringement.

Axel Scheffler says he wants better protection for creative works

Scheffler, who does not own a smartphone, said he tried to ignore AI until someone showed him how his most famous creations had been digitally recreated in locations such as Silicon Valley and Oktoberfest.

"I was quite shocked. It's clearly my mouse, my Gruffalo, as close as they can do it, but the rest of the image is completely created - it's a clear theft of copyright," he told the BBC.

Scheffler is considering launching the legal action in Germany because he believes the European Union is more creator-friendly.

Nick Buckland, an intellectual property lawyer at London firm Lewis Silkin, agreed that Germany could offer a route for creators seeking to protect their work.

"There have been two cases in Germany where music collecting societies have been able to win against AI companies by showing that those AI companies have copied lyrics of songs verbatim and have presented them," he told the BBC.

But proving copyright infringement could be difficult, he said.

While having a distinctive character such as the Gruffalo could help Scheffler's case, he would need to establish that his copyright had been infringed.

"Generative AI doesn't copy, it trains," Buckland explained.

"This is what AI companies say means that they're not infringing someone's copyright.

"For example, if someone wants a picture of a dog, what the AI machine does is it scans everything it's trained on, millions of pictures of dogs, and then one gets presented to the user."

Nick Buckland said proving copyright infringement would not be straightforward

OpenAI, the company behind ChatGPT, is already being sued by German publishing group Penguin Random House, together with author and illustrator Ingo Siegner.

The allegation is that OpenAI copied the children's book character The Little Dragon Coconut (Der kleine Drache Kokosnuss)

Whether the AI company has breached copyright law will be decided by the Munich Regional Court in spring 2027.

Carina Mathern, children's and young adult books publisher and member of the management board of Penguin Random House publishing group, said: "Through this lawsuit, we... want to help ensure that copyright remains effectively protected in the age of artificial intelligence and that fair conditions are secured for creative professionals."

An OpenAI spokesperson said: "We're having productive conversations with rightsholders around the world about supporting creativity, including fan art, while protecting intellectual property and taking appropriate action in response to copyright complaints."

The California-based firm said its models were trained in various sources and that copyright holders could submit disputes directly with them.

온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

마치 테러리스트가 인질극 벌이는데 인질 죽는다고 테러리스트 진압 안하겠다는 것과 같은 말이다.

총수, 의장 검찰 총원해서 조져 놓다가 사면을 해놓으니까 버릇이 안좋아 진건지 아니면 반도체좀 했다고 뭐가 된양인지 모르겠다만

앞으로 대한민국에서도 여당과 야당 합작으로 대기업 총수, 의장 사법처리하고 사면하지않고 만기 출소하는 케이스가 단 한 번이라도 나와서 명확하게 그 선례를 남겨놔야한다는게 내 생

I run a few models on my machine, from the dumb 9B one to the quantized big ones . All my models run in an isolated environment (not like ClosedAI … real isolation). The network passes through a small checklist before leaving my machine, and each environment has its own files, almost like a virtual machine inside my machine. For the technical folks, I have a few containers running.

This is partly because I’m using smaller models, which frequently hallucinate or make wrong changes. But it’s also to stop the owner of the mechanical parrot from knowing too much about my host machine, especially after the latest round of AI security circus show . From their side, it’s just an isolated VPS with the project, no environment, no variables.

Nice. So I use the safer approach that I’ve already discussed and tested in the past.

Yeah, keep in mind that LLMs are part of AI, but AI is a much bigger field, and calling LLMs the same as AI is wrong. Another topic that I’ve already dipped my toes into. So if you have a spell checker in your text editor, you are using AI. If you have played any video game with a simple decision tree, it’s also AI. So don’t get me wrong, but I use AI.

I'm doing okay. I may choose to approve this candidate...They’re far above average; I see no need to explore other parts of this profile—this is the best I can find

For study? Sure. For writing, also sure. I’m not a native English speaker, so having a spellchecker isn’t always enough. Sometimes I need to validate if the grammar I used works in the sentence that I created. Often it does, but sometimes the Latino blood speaks louder and I need to revalidate the whole sentence.

Let me start with handcraft . This is the art of doing it yourself. It means not using most of the automated tools. I’m not saying you should write your own OS from scratch or bake your own silicon. But it does mean avoiding the auto-generation Photoshop tool in favor of cloning and hand-painting the photos.

It’s writing the code yourself, not using a language server ( if you don’t know what a language server is… I’ve bad news… ), and avoiding code generation tools like the rails…

items.title: LLM Voice
items.content:
Sometimes when I read a post, I get the growing feeling that I'm reading

the output of an LLM. I can't necessarily define why, although there are the common

tells (it's not the em-dashes, it's the load-bearing tapestries). As I

do this my desire to read on atrophies, sometimes to the point of revulsion

There are tools out there that claim to be able to tell the difference

between LLM-written prose and the old-fashioned biological product. I'm wary

of them, partly due skeptism about their accuracy, but also because it rather

misses the point. The reaction to LLM-Voice is a human one, that sense that we

valley of prose. By the time I'd reach for a tool to tell me what I'm

reading, it's already too late, even if it confidently tells me there's no LLM

I'm also suspicious of my own ability to accurately recognize LLM voice. Language

changes over time, so a common sign of age is complaining about the language

of the youngs. I'm inclined to bristle at prose that talks about “adopting a

new sales motion ,” or “a sharp round-up of news”. But I've heard

these constructs coming out of human mouths, so that's more a generational

difference rather than between carbon and silicon. (And as a transplanted Brit,

don't get me started on Americanisms, I'm sure I'll get used to them momentarily.)

Right now I urge authors to be extra-wary of LLM-Voice. In particular I

strongly recommend that authors should not fall into the trap of getting the

LLM to write a draft. Even if it's edited by a human, it's very hard to expel

the LLM-Voice - thus causing the uncanny valley reaction. 1 Even accepting suggestions of rephrasing is dangerous. I

have heard of people using LLMs to develop outline and structure, that

may be ok, but only as far as an outline. 2

Authors should fill the prose themselves.

Very hard, but not impossible. I've come across one case where I do know

the first draft was entirely done by LLM, but I detected no LLM Voice when

I read the final piece. It did, however, need a professional editor at a

major periodical publication to clean it up.

My policy on this site, is that anyone who uses AI to help them write

should declare how they used it, usually in the

acknowledgments. This is partly for transparency, and partly so that

readers can learn useful ways to use AI. In my own case, I don't use AI

for generating prose, nor for help in structure. The only way I use it for

writing is as a search tool (but I verify any information by going

even more important in the age of LLMs. I habitually speak the words in my head

and then write them down (and then edit what I've just written). This advice

is particularly important to anyone who has any desire to communicate

regularly with writing. Like many things, learning to be a good writer relies

on lots of practice. It's a skill worth the time to acquire, but surrendering

In time it may be that LLMs will be so good that we can't tell the

difference. In many ways, that's more worrying. Like most writers, I find

writing an almost-essential tool for thinking. Often it's only by writing

something down, that I can really get my thoughts on a topic into coherence.

I've often started an essay knowing I don't really understand something, but

the act of wrestling with the words forces me to overcome my confusions. As

more people delegate writing to LLMs they will also delegate thinking and

comprehension to LLMs. I don't want to do that, where's the fun of writing then?

Although avoiding LLM-Voice is a general rule, it isn't an absolute one. An

important example is that of Jim Highsmith (who contributes to this site). He

finds working with an LLM is essential to his writing to overcome the bane of Parkinson's

disease . I'll gladly deal with LLM-Voice in order to continue imbibing my

comfortable in English, it is their second or fourth language. Some have found

From curl 8.12 through 8.16, config files could slice variable values and include other config files without an explicit depth cap. Curl 8.17.0 added a five-level include cap that breaks this reduction.

items.summary_ko: curl 8.12부터 8.16까지는 설정 파일이 변수 값을 자르고 다른 설정 파일을 포함할 수 있었으며, 포함 깊이에 명시적 제한이 없었다. 이 기능들로 두 개의 카운터를 가진 Minsky 프로그램을 흉내 낼 수 있었고, 문자열과 자원이 무제한이라는 가정 아래 튜링 완전했다. curl 8.17.0이 포함(include)을 다섯 단계로 제한하면서 이 구성은 깨졌다.
items.content_ko: 카운터 값 n은 x의 n개 복사본으로 표현되며, 각 명령 상태는 파일 이름을 레이블로 삼는 하나 이상의 설정 파일로 구현된다. 이 방식으로 두 카운터 프로그램을 curl 설정 파일로 컴파일할 수 있다. 예시로 2 + 3을 계산하는 파일 네 개가 제공된다. 다만 이 환원은 무제한 카운터와 무제한 단계를 가정하며, 실제 바이너리에는 그런 자원이 없다. items.title: Nissan says Oracle PeopleSoft break-in may have spilled payroll records, SSNs
items.content:
Nissan says Oracle PeopleSoft break-in may have spilled payroll records, SSNs

Carmaker points finger at an 'unknown' flaw as customer fallout continues

Nissan has joined the growing list of Oracle customers cleaning up after a cyberattack, warning employees that payroll records, bank details, Social Security numbers, and other personal data may have been stolen.

In a filing submitted to the California Attorney General on Friday, Nissan Americas said Oracle had informed it of "a cyber event" involving the personnel records of "hundreds of companies." The automaker said it later learned Nissan had been "specifically targeted" in the attack.

A notification sent to current and former employees, seen by The Register , says the company believes attackers accessed a haul of sensitive info, including contact and banking information; Social Security, Social Insurance, or other national identification numbers; financial and tax records; and dependent and beneficiary details.

Current and former employees in the US, Canada, Mexico, and Brazil may have been affected, although Nissan said it is still working to determine exactly whose information was exposed.

Nissan said it kicked off its incident response plan after learning of the intrusion, brought in outside security specialists, and has been working with Oracle while keeping law enforcement informed. It plans to offer affected individuals credit or dark web monitoring where available.

The company has also put a few extra locks on the payroll office. Employees can now access pay slips or update direct deposit details only from a corporate network or through a secure VPN, while Nissan adds extra identity checks before processing payroll requests.

The accompanying employee FAQ pins the incident on "an unknown vulnerability in Oracle's PeopleSoft software" and says the campaign is affecting "hundreds of companies and institutions." The document offers no clue as to what the vulnerability is, whether Oracle has patched it, or whether the compromised PeopleSoft environment was hosted by Oracle or by Nissan itself.

The disclosure lands just weeks after researchers linked the ShinyHunters extortion crew to a wave of attacks exploiting a PeopleSoft zero-day . More than 100 organizations and roughly 300 PeopleSoft instances were reportedly compromised before Oracle issued mitigation measures, with the gang claiming to have made off with HR, payroll, and other enterprise data.

Weak security means attackers could disable all of a city's public EV chargers

US regulator tells GM to hit the brakes on customer tracking

21K Nissan customers' data stolen in Red Hat raid

Porsche panic in Russia as pricey status symbols forget how to car

Oracle has said little publicly about the reported attacks and didn't respond to The Register's questions, even as organizations have continued to disclose being caught in the fallout.

Nissan has not confirmed that the incidents are connected, though its California filing lists the breach period as May 27 through June 9, broadly aligning with the previously reported timeline.

The carmaker didn't respond to questions about how many current and former employees are affected, when Oracle first notified it of the breach, and whether the compromise was limited to Oracle-managed systems. ®

items.title: Trump ignored intel on China’s Nvidia spy to protect company’s stock, report says: Spy accused of exploiting Trump ties to Huang, funneling secrets to China.
items.content:
Donald Trump apparently is so aligned with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang—who has become the president’s key advisor on AI —that he ignored intelligence indicating that Huang was the target of a “Chinese spy plot,” and did so partly to protect Nvidia’s stock.

The New York Times spoke with people briefed on US intelligence agencies’ surveillance and granted them anonymity to discuss findings drawn from “classified intelligence.” According to sources, about a year ago, Trump was briefed that “Beijing was getting reports from someone with direct access” to Huang. That “someone” was Alice Huang, or Huang Le, a Chinese citizen and former top executive at a Singapore cloud company called Megaspeed.

According to sources, the US had already suspected that Alice Huang—who is not related to Jensen Huang—was helping China evade export controls to gain access to high-end Nvidia chips through Megaspeed. But it alarmed investigators to discover that she may have used her role at Megaspeed to gain direct access to Jensen Huang. It’s now believed she may have leveraged that closeness to feed China intel not only on one of America’s leading AI companies, but also to influence Trump’s thinking on AI. As Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent noted last month ahead of Trump’s AI talks with China President Xi Jinping, “the president is completely aligned with Jensen Huang, the CEO of Nvidia.”

At least partly due to fears that US action against the alleged spying could hobble Nvidia chip sales or disrupt the delicate US-China trade truce, Trump “chose not to do anything with the information,” sources said.

Soon after US scrutiny increased, Alice Huang’s name was removed from Megaspeed corporate documents. At this stage, it’s unclear “how closely she is still connected to Megaspeed,” NYT reported.

Liu Chang, the spokesperson for the Chinese Embassy in Washington, DC, told NYT that the US accusations against Alice Huang are baseless. He accused the US of pursuing a campaign of “groundless smears and slanders” against China.

It’s not clear which agencies were investigating Alice Huang or what triggered their suspicions, NYT reported. Sources also could not explain what information she may have shared with Beijing.

Nvidia has denied that she would have had access to any trade secrets, but it seems notable that Jensen Huang did not receive a defensive briefing that Americans sometimes get when they’re targets of foreign spying. Some senior officials think it’s unlikely that Jensen Huang would have “remained unaware” of Alice Huang’s alleged intelligence-gathering for the entire duration of their professional relationship, although Trump was told Jensen Huang had no knowledge at the time of his briefing. It seems possible that Jensen Huang got no briefing because US agencies worried that he might tip her off that “she was being watched,” the NYT reported.

Trump’s deep ties with tech leaders have been criticized throughout his administration, but Jensen Huang’s influence increasingly stands out . To critics, the political friendship appears to be largely based on growing his business in China. Since cozying up to Trump, the Nvidia CEO has gotten export controls relaxed and even struck a controversial deal giving the US a 25 percent cut of some chip sales  so he could try to sell more chips in China. Sources told NYT that “some investigations and proposed trade sanctions involving China or Nvidia” have “ground to a halt within the Commerce Department” due to Jensen Huang’s influence.

No one’s sure when Jensen Huang met Alice Huang, but NYT found social media photos that predated her role arranging a Megaspeed purchase of $2 billion in chips over the next year. If those chips ended up in China, the US worried they “could help adversaries like China develop new weapons, surveil dissidents, and leap ahead of the United States in AI development,” NYT reported. items.title: A select should tell you something
items.content:
Heads up: your browser doesn’t support customizable selects yet, so the “after” demos below look like ordinary selects. That’s also exactly what your visitors would see in this browser. To see the difference, open this page in Chrome or Edge.

There are multiple articles about appearance: base-select and how you can use it. We finally can style a select. The bigger change is what an option can hold. Until now, an option was one line of plain text, so everything a person needed to decide had to fit in a label or be left out. Now an option can carry the thing people actually decide with: a preview, a number, a job title, a warning. They stop reading and working things out, and start recognising.

Below are five selects, each shown before and after. The before is what most forms do today. The after is the same <select> , with the same keyboard behaviour and the same form value. Only what it shows has changed. If you want the mechanics, the Chrome team’s announcement and MDN’s guide cover them well.

A font picker usually lists names. To choose well, you either already know what Fraunces looks like, or you pick it, look at the result, and come back to try the next one.

When each option is set in its own typeface, the option is the preview. You judge the shape, not the name.

This pattern is not new. We already have in document editors (like Google Docs) and in design tools (like Figma and Photoshop). It just became available for us and all we need is one inline style per option, style="font-family: 'Fraunces', serif" , and the closed control keeps the typeface after you choose. We are also able to show the category of each font, like Serif, Sans, Mono, Display, or Handwriting.

Time zone pickers tend to look like “(GMT+09:00) Tokyo”. The offset is accurate and almost never what you want. What you want is the time there, so you add the offset to your own time in your head, and maybe get it wrong around midnight.

Show the current time next to each city, plus whether it’s day or night, and the question answers itself before you choose.

This is the only demo that needs JavaScript, because the times come from Intl.DateTimeFormat .

Delivery options are usually a group of radio buttons, each with its details written out as a sentence.

To be fair, radio buttons have a real strength. Every option is visible without a click, and for two or three short choices they’re the right pattern. But once each option carries a few facts, the facts end up in prose. Comparing means reading every sentence and holding the numbers in your head.

A select with the facts in aligned columns turns that into a glance down a column, in the space of a single field.

At a company of about two hundred people, we had two colleagues with the same name, in different departments. Whenever I had to pick one of them, I went by their job title. Photos help less than you’d think, because people often don’t know what a colleague looks like, especially one in another department.

A text-only select gives you two identical options and a guess. Put the title and department under each name and they become two different answers. The closed control keeps the title too, so anyone reviewing the form can see who you picked.

Some options come with consequences. In a plain select, you find out afterwards.

Mark those options in the list and you know while you’re choosing.

The badge appears only on the options that require special attention, and nowhere else.

Every “after” in this post is a plain <select> . Keyboard handling, type-to-jump, form submission, select.value , required , validation and the accessible role all stay with the browser, and the control itself needs no JavaScript.

The bigger trade-off is on phones. A native select opens the operating system’s own picker. It shows a scrolling wheel on iOS, a sheet on Android. Those are familiar, sized for thumbs, and tuned to each platform’s accessibility features. A customizable select doesn’t use them; it draws its own…

온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

items.title: H.264 Is Magic (2016)
items.content:
H.264 is a video compression codec standard. It is ubiquitous - internet video, Blu-ray, phones, security cameras, drones, everything. Everything uses H.264 now.

H.264 is a remarkable piece of technology. It is the result of 30+ years of work with one single goal: To reduce the bandwidth required for transmission of full-motion video.

Technically, it is very interesting. This post will give insight into some of the details at a high level - I hope to not bore you too much with the intricacies. Also note that many of the concepts explained here apply to video compression in general, and not just H.264.

A simple uncompressed video file will contain an array of 2D buffers containing pixel data for each frame. So it's a 3D (2 spatial dimensions and 1 temporal) array of bytes. Each pixel takes 3 bytes to store - one byte each for the three primary colors (red, green and blue).

1080p @ 60 Hz = 1920x1080x60x3 => ~ 370 MB/sec of raw data.

This is next to impossible to deal with. A 50GB Blu-ray disk will only hold ~2 mins. You can't move it anywhere fast. Even SSDs have trouble dumping this straight from RAM to Disk[^1].

Yes, I will answer this. But first let me show you something. Here is the Apple Homepage:

I captured the screen of this home page and produced two files:

PNG screenshot of the Apple homepage 1015KB

5 Second 60fps H.264 video of the same Apple homepage 175KB

Eh. What? Those file sizes look switched.

No, they're right. The H.264 video, 300 frames long is 175KB. A single frame of that video in PNG is 1015KB.

It looks like we're storing 300 times the amount of data in the video. But the file size is a fifth. So H.264 would seem to be 1500x as efficient as PNG.

How is this even possible? All right, what's the trick?

There are very many tricks! H.264 uses all the tricks you can think of (and tons you can't think of). Let's go through the important ones.

Imagine you're building a car for street racing. You need to go faster. What is the first thing you do? You shed some weight. Your car weighs 3000 lbs. You throw away stuff you don't need. Those back seats? pfft. Chuck those. That subwoofer? Gone. No music for you. Air Conditioning? Yeah, ditch it. Transmission? Ye..no. Wait! We're gonna need that.

You remove everything except the things that matter.

This concept of throwing away bits you don't need to save space is called lossy compression. H.264 is a lossy codec - it throws away less important bits and only keeps the important bits.

PNG is a lossless codec. It means that nothing is thrown away. Bit for bit, the original source image can be recovered from a PNG encoded image.

Important bits? How does the algorithm know what bits in my frame are important?

There are few obvious ways to trim out images. Maybe the top right quadrant is useless all the time. So maybe we can zero out those pixels and discard that quadrant. We would use only 3/4th of the space we need. ~2200 lbs now. Or maybe we can crop out a thick border around the edges of the frame, the important stuff is in the middle anyway. Yes, you could do these. But H.264 doesn't do this.

H.264, like other lossy image algorithms, discards detail information. Here is a close-up of the original compared with the image post-discard.

See how the compressed one does not show the holes in the speaker grills in the MacBook Pro? If you don't zoom in, you would even notice the difference. The image on the right weighs in at 7% the size of the original - and we haven't even compressed the image in the traditional sense. Imagine your car weighed just 200 lbs!

7% wow! How do you discard detail information like that?

Now we're getting to the juicy bits! Ha puns! If you took an information theory class, you might remember information entropy. Information entropy is the number of bits required to represent some information. Note that it is not simply the size of some dataset. It is minimum number of bits that must be used to represent all the information…

items.content_ko: 비압축 영상은 프레임마다 픽셀 2차원 버퍼가 쌓인 3차원 배열이고, 픽셀 하나당 빨강·초록·파랑 각 1바이트, 총 3바이트가 필요하다. 이런 원시 영상은 저장과 전송 모두 감당하기 어려우며, SSD조차 RAM에서 디스크로 바로 옮기는 데 어려움을 겪는다. 글쓴이는 H.264의 기법을 고수준에서 소개하며, 여기서 설명하는 개념들은 H.264뿐 아니라 비디오 압축 일반에 적용된다고 밝힌다. 본문은 도입부에서 끊겨 있다.

items.title: C2PA's eMudhra Moment
items.summary: cryptography, security
items.content:
By David Buchanan (aka retr0id), 29 th October 2026

The eMudhra incident has shown how the modern Web PKI ecosystem reacts to a CA compromise. All things considered, I think it went smoothly—all the web browsers I use picked up the revocations swiftly. But it has also been a clusterfuck, with eMudhra trying to downplay their responsibilities and refusing to elaborate on how exactly the failure occurred. There's also a long tail of TLS clients that don't have a great way to handle revocations, or are otherwise not getting their trust stores updated in a timely manner.

The C2PA ecosystem tries to solve a very similar problem to Web PKI, but it is comparatively in its infancy. The media verification tools you'll find in search result top-spots today don't support revocation-checking at all.

So how would the C2PA ecosystem react to a similar compromise? Let's find out!

The above demonstrates a S/MIME encrypted message, with a signature that chains to Google's C2PA root CA, which is in the official C2PA trust list .

The vulnerabilities I exploited to produce this chain are not eligible for bug bounty rewards, and are in fact already publicly known. But in the spirit of our little experiment I'm not going to elaborate.

The astute observer will note that my demo is "not the same" as the eMudhra compromise, because it's merely a leaf cert that has a private key of 4, rather than a trusted intermediate.

I can get Google's intermediate to sign any leaf key I like (via an undisclosed method), and that "4" key is just how I'm proving it.

In the context of TLS that's kinda how cert issuance works normally, but it completely breaks the C2PA trust model .

C2PA 생태계는 아직 초기 단계라서, 검색 상위에 노출되는 미디어 검증 도구들은 폐기 확인을 전혀 지원하지 않는다. 글쓴이는 Google의 C2PA 루트 CA에 체인되는 S/MIME 암호화 메시지를 시연한다. 이 체인을 만들기 위해 악용한 취약점은 버그 바운티 대상이 아니며 이미 공개되어 있다고 밝힌다. 원문이 중간에서 끊겨 있다.

items.title: Chinese Hackers Abused Google Workspace Rules to Steal Research and Defense Emails
items.content:
A China-linked espionage group hid inside North American medical, academic, and military research networks for more than a year, quietly stealing sensitive research and defense email.

The way in was a backdoor on their REDCap research servers that stole login credentials. The exfiltration was the unusual part: the attackers rewired the victims' own Google Workspace rules to copy any message matching their keywords to an inbox they controlled.

Google's Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) laid out the campaign in a report published this week and attributes it with high confidence to a cluster it tracks as UNC6508.

The actor and its REDCap backdoor are not new names; Google first surfaced both in February , in a wider report on state-backed attacks against the defense sector. It did not name the victims, describing them only as multiple organizations across the US and Canada: clinical providers, academic centers, military health institutions, advocacy groups, and health regulators.

Google says it notified them and disrupted the group's infrastructure.

The entry point was REDCap (Research Electronic Data Capture), a web platform that hospitals and universities use to build and manage study databases. UNC6508 compromised externally facing REDCap servers.

Google has not pinned down the initial access vector, named a specific CVE, or listed the affected versions, though it saw the group probing older, vulnerable ones.

Around three months after getting in, the group deployed custom malware GTIG calls INFINITERED , which trojanizes REDCap's own system files and does three things.

The earliest known compromise dates to September 2023, with activity continuing through November 2025. Once on the server, UNC6508 ran internal reconnaissance and credential discovery, pulling database and service account credentials, then used those logins to move into the internal network and on to a domain administrator account.

Google does not spell out the exact path to that admin account. With admin rights, the group set up the exfiltration.

The exfiltration rode a feature that was already there. UNC6508 abused content compliance rules, a legitimate Google Workspace admin feature that scans mail for keywords and can copy or forward matching messages.

Similar features exist in other cloud mail suites. The group created a rule, misspelled "Patroit," that watched for nearly 150 keywords, search terms, and email addresses. When a message matched, Workspace silently BCC'd it to an attacker-controlled Gmail address, which Google has since disabled. No malware on the mail server, no separate exfiltration tool, no unusual network traffic. Just a built-in mail feature, turned to copy the organization's secrets to an inbox the attackers owned.

MITRE already catalogs email-forwarding-rule abuse as a known technique. What GTIG flags as new here is the use of domain content compliance rules to do it, a method it says it had not seen from a China-linked actor before.

The rule's keywords mapped to UNC6508's collection priorities: geo-strategic policy, military strategy and equipment, advanced technology including AI and uncrewed vehicles, offensive cyber programs, and medical research. One term stood out for its specificity, chikungunya , the mosquito-borne virus behind a 2025 outbreak in China's Guangdong province.

Start with REDCap. Patch externally facing servers and remove old versions outright, not just alongside the current build. REDCap lets legacy versions run side-by-side, and that is what enables downgrade attacks, where an attacker forces software back to a known-vulnerable release.

Then check the mail side. Review Workspace, or equivalent, content compliance and mail-forwarding rules for anything that BCCs or reroutes mail to outside addresses. Check admin audit logs for when rules changed, not just what they say now. Pull GTIG's published indicators and hunt for INFINITERED. Binance is the world’s largest cryptocurrency trading platform by volume, with hundreds of thousands of users. Brent Lewin / Bloomberg via Getty

Oct. 29, 2026, 6:46 PM EDT  /  Updated   Oct. 29, 2026, 11:31 PM EDT

The digital currency exchange Binance says it was the target of a $6.3 billion crypto heist Thursday, believed to be the largest ever recorded.

The company has suspended all deposits and withdrawals while it works with law enforcement to secure its infrastructure and locate stolen funds.

The hack originated from a compromised laptop, it said, which allowed “an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions.”

“The estimated total impact sits at around $6.3B,” Binance said late Thursday on X .

About $3 billion of crypto assets that transited through wallets connected to the hackers have so far been identified and frozen, the company said.

Binance will “cover all losses” from the hack, it said, adding, “User funds are safe.”

“We are working closely with our law enforcement partners to confirm the identity of these criminals and bring them to justice,” it said.

items.content:
온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

items.title: HP Poly VoIP vulnerability sets the stage for executive voice deepfakes
items.content:
HP has released patches for a critical buffer overflow vulnerability in multiple IP-enabled conference phones from its Poly Voice line. The flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to obtain root privileges on the underlying operating system, potentially enabling them to execute other attacks such as eavesdropping on conversations and recording voice data for AI-enabled impersonation attacks.

The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-0826 , was discovered by researchers from security firm Rapid7 and resides in the code that parses Session Description Protocol (SDP) attributes when the Interactive Connectivity Establishment (ICE) feature is enabled.

ICE enables VoIP devices to establish peer-to-peer connections using the shortest available network path. The feature is not enabled by default on HP Poly devices, and the company advises administrators to disable it if it’s not needed.

The flaw, rated 9.2 on the CVSS severity scale, affects all phones from the HP Poly VVX series, as well as the Trio 8300, 8500, and 8800 IP conference devices. HP has fixed the flaw in its Poly Unified Communications Software (UCS) versions 6.4.8 for the VVX devices, 8.1.7 for the Trio 8300, and 7.2.8 for Trio 8500 and 8800.

An exploit module targeting this vulnerability has already been developed and released for the widely used Metasploit penetration testing framework that’s maintained by Rapid7.

The exploit executes code as root on an affected device with ICE enabled by sending a SIP INVITE request with a specially crafted candidate attribute. This attribute normally contains a transport address that can be used for connectivity checks and is part of the ICE RFC8839 standard.

The buffer overflow bug is located in a helper function called ParseICECandidate in the polyapp binary that processes such requests on the device.

“The start of the function contains a call to memcpy , which will copy the incoming string line being processed into a 256 byte stack buffer,” Stephen Fewer, senior principal security researcher at Rapid7, said in a blog post . “No length check is performed to ensure the incoming string length is less than 256 bytes. Therefore by providing a candidate attribute whose length is greater than 256 bytes, a stack-based buffer overflow will occur.”

Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR), a kernel feature that randomizes memory addresses to defeat buffer overflow exploits, is enabled on the device. However, the protection is not operating correctly on the HP Poly devices because it does not randomize the load addresses of .so (Shared Object) libraries.

These libraries, such as libc , are loaded by other processes, including the polyapp process, and because their memory addresses never change, they can be leveraged to bypass ASLR and execute the attacker’s payload.

“We create a ROP chain that will execute an arbitrary OS command via the system standard C library function,” Fewer said. “The accompanying Metasploit exploit modules source code details the entire ROP chain.”

Attackers have increasingly targeted embedded devices inside enterprise networks in recent years because unlike laptops, workstations, and servers, these devices are not monitored by endpoint detection and response (EDR) products. As such, they provide perfect footholds inside corporate environments that allow attackers to remain undetected for long periods of time and attack other systems.

In the age of AI these devices become even more relevant for attackers, going beyond corporate espionage by recording conversations or internal network pivoting.

“Attackers no longer need massive datasets to make use of synthetic speech tooling,” Douglas McKee, Rapid7’s director of vulnerability intelligence, said in a blog post . “In many cases, they just need clean source audio of the right person saying enough words in enough contexts. That has made executive voice data, call recordings, and live conversation capture far more valuable than many organizations seem prepared…

items.title: Attacker gets away with up to $3 billion from Binance
items.content:
A notorious North Korean cybercrime group has stolen around $6.3 billion in cryptoassets from multiple hot wallets a belonging to Binance, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, and still controls around $3 billion of it after stablecoin issuers and other protocols froze what they could. These estimates are still in flux as various platforms work to freeze tokens or otherwise thwart the attacker from cashing out, and as both Binance and independent security researchers continue their investigations.

Unlike many supposedly “multi-billion dollar” crypto hacks, where the headline figure relies on the notional value of illiquid assets that could never be sold for anywhere near that amount, the majority of these stolen assets were major stablecoins, bitcoin, ethereum, and other fairly liquid tokens.

(via Arkham ) Binance has estimated the total theft at $6.3 billion. At least $5.5 billion of these were liquid assets. Tether announced they had frozen at least $1.567 billion of the stolen USDT, and Circle has frozen around $800 million of stolen USDC. World Liberty Financial froze the $27 million in USD1 stolen by the attacker, and the Arbitrum ethereum layer-2 network froze an additional $30.5 million that had moved to its network. The attacker is estimated to have made off with between $2.4 billion and $3.3 billion .

Binance founder Changpeng Zhao, who is legally not allowed to have any active role with the company [ I98 ] yet still has remarkable amounts of inside knowledge into its inner workings, posted on Twitter less than an hour after the theft that “User funds are safe!”, adding early estimates of how much Tether and Circle had frozen. He added, “I don't manage Binance (.com) anymore, but as a shareholder, I expect all user funds will be fully covered.”

Tweet by Changpeng Zhao He later tweeted “Loss might be a bit higher than [$1 billion], but will cover.” (Why a person who is barred from any control over Binance would be the one promising this is an exercise I will leave to the reader.)

Binance keeps an emergency insurance fund in case of exploits or other crypto disasters. Its most recent balance report puts it at around $1.3 billion. 1 Unless more is recovered, Binance will either fail to make users whole or dip into its own balance sheet — potentially to the tune of 10 figures.

Binance later wrote that their "initial investigation suggests that the security incident may involve a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop", which allowed an attacker to “submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions.” They estimated the total theft at around $6.3 billion, with approximately $3 billion frozen. 2 While the assets frozen by Tether and Circle will likely easily be returned to Binance, other non-centralized assets frozen by various protocols may be inaccessible both to the attacker and to Binance.

Blockchain security firm TRM Labs has attributed the theft to TraderTraitor, a North Korean state-sponsored cybercrime group also known as the Lazarus Group. 3 The group has been linked to other massive cryptocurrency heists, including a massive $1.5 billion theft from the Bybit cryptocurrency exchange in 2025 [ W3IGG ]. This Binance hack has now surpassed the Bybit hack for the largest cryptocurrency theft.

The contagion also threatens to spread beyond Binance. Aave, a defi lending project, paused some of its markets to stop the attacker from depositing stolen assets as collateral and borrowing against them — a move that could otherwise leave it holding significant bad debt. Protocols that are slower to respond may not be so lucky.

The Binance theft came within hours of a separate, much smaller theft of around $2.7 million from Polymarket users [ W3IGG ], and some people wondered whether the two were connected. I doubt it. Polymarket has blamed its incident on a compromised third-party vendor, which an attacker apparently used to inject a malicious script into the site’s frontend and steal user funds. items.title: Quirks and Vintage Uses of CSS Table Display
items.content:
I’ve long found the ability to use layouts of table elements with CSS rather odd. In addition to well known and loved values of CSS ’ display property, like block , inline , flex , and grid , there are values like table and table-cell . What do these values do and why would they be used?

The syntax for table markup is well known. <table> wraps the table, <thead> contains the table’s header row, and is full of <th> elements which hold each header cell content, <tbody> contains the table’s body rows, <tr> holds an individual table row, and <td> is a cell of table data within a row. Then <colgroup> and <col> are used together to define a group of columns. <caption> can provide an accessible name and description for a table and <tfoot> can provide a footer.

All these table elements are semantic – they have meaning. Unlike a <div> or <span> they all have roles which browsers and other technologies understand. All the table-related elements are specifically designed for tabular data (two-dimensional presentation of rows and columns containing cells). As the HTML Living Standard describes, a <tr> , for example, has an ARIA role of row . Other table elements take different roles based on their purpose.

This might not make much difference from a cursory glance, but it has major impact on how assistive technologies interpret and parse a table. HTML tables are a fickle thing to meddle with and are nigh-impossible to reimplement with any other elements in a way equivalent to the real thing. However, their layout capabilities have many other uses beyond tabular data. Most of these uses are better achieved with other web platform features, but during the 2000s and early/mid 2010s, they were a go-to way to achieve many layouts.

In almost every case, semantic HTML elements should be used to markup a table. They’re fit for purpose for tabular data and universally supported. If you’re making a table to be used as a table, make it a <table> . However, CSS has many table-related values for the display property:

table - behave like <table> (with the same block-level box).

inline table - behave like <table> but with an inline-level box rather than a block-level box like a typical <table> .

inline-table - legacy precomposed syntax from CSS 2 that is equivalent to inline table .

table-column-group - behave like <colgroup> .

table-footer-group - behave like <tfoot> .

table-header-group - behave like <thead> .

These values don’t actually assign the semantic role of a table – just the layout. As such, they can be used for the benefits of table layout without the baked-in condition of tabular data.

In the days of responsive design before flexbox and grid, these display values would sometimes be used during the table layout era to facilitate usage of the same HTML markup between desktop and mobile viewports. On desktop a full table layout could be used. On mobile inline layouts could be used without having to change the markup. As the table layout was only defined in CSS , there were no HTML -related semantics clashes involved in trying to void the table element’s roles for a non-table application. Generic tags could be used and the layout toggled with CSS .

You could apply a table layout to <div> soup using CSS :

Regular block elements don’t share heights, so developers would set display: table on a wrapper element, followed by display: table-cell on the children to prompt the children to stretch to match the height of the tallest element in the row. This would work because browsers force a strict hierarchy for table layout. A table-cell must be within a table-row , so if it isn’t, the browser generates an anonymous box as a sort of error-correction to make the layout function. Then, the standard styling of tables where all cells in different columns on the same row have the height of the tallest cell applies.

items.title: Shared password manager for families?
items.summary: ask, security
items.content:
Long story short, I need to have a bunch of shared accounts with family for finance and insurance and stuff, mostly for the sake of family members who are getting old and need help keeping things organized. So the requirements are:

I would just use 1Password, but recent events have demonstrated them as not exactly competent. I could always use KeepassXC and keep the file in a Google Drive folder, or maybe teach my siblings to use Syncthing, but that feels like extra steps we could do without. Anyone have any recommendations for how to do this well?

If you can selfhost I'd recommend looking at Vaultwarden . They support sharing credentials in groups and emergency access conditions, which have proved useful to me and my family in the past. The apps/integrations (Android, iOS, Browsers, Desktop, CLI) are provided by Bitwarden and they are available cross platform.

That's what I'm using right now, and it's great. I'm not switching away yet, but Bitwarden's recent license changes for their clients have made the hairs on the back of my neck stand up.

So far, it's not a pressing concern for me, but it's made me slightly less eager to recommend my setup to others. I hope they maintain the status quo.

Here's the license change details for those who, like me, missed it: https://community.bitwarden.com/t/published-version-update-in-app-stores/102750/7

Same boat here. So far I'm still happy with my setup but it feels like it's on borrowed time. There may be a point where a community fork is inevitable.

I have my hopes high with things like rbw already out there.

I second vaultwarden, the bitwarden modules are useful & easy to understand (tested on android & firefox).

+1 I use the saas / online version for my family and it has worked well for us.

I host vaultwarden at home reachable via wirguard. Works really great.

I would just use 1Password, but recent events have demonstrated them as not exactly competent.

1password didn't fix clickjacking attack vulnerability (reported in April last year) over 4 months before disclosure (August last year) and it still wasn't fixed in January this year. I didn't take time to check whether it's still the case

That doesn’t seem like a big deal to me.

I'd say any known attack for a password manager is big HUGE, no matter the prerequisites

They also sponsor DHH's Omarchy, which is why I switched to Bitwarden.

Would simply Apple Passwords work? The sharing feature is great

I accepted to migrate my phone/laptop to Apple in order to simplify this type of situation around Apple tools for family, subscriptions and passwords sharing. The last part I am not convinced is regarding mail management. For now, everyone keeps their but I would like to have a shared set-up in the future.

I use KeepassXC with Syncthing for personal and team databases, the only downside of it is merge conflicts, but I'm not really worried about it as it doesn't happen often and syncthing keeps the conflict so i wont lose the data

But the bigger challenge is sharing the second factor ( email token, phone token, passkey , 2fa ). And every app now has a unique process that is constantly changing. You can’t plan ahead of time

If you pay for Bitwarden, you can store TOTP codes in it, at least. If the email credentials are in the vault you can get email tokens too. SMS is the only one that would be troublesome.

items.title: Linux Kernel TCP Flaw With 9.8 CVSS Score Affects Ubuntu, Red Hat and Other Distributions
items.content:
A flaw in the Linux kernel's TCP code, tracked as CVE-2026-98432 , affects Ubuntu, Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL), and other Linux distributions. The kernel's own CVE team rates it 9.8 out of 10 on the CVSS scale.

Anthropic said on October 27 that its AI model wrote an exploit that uses the flaw to let a remote attacker with no credentials run commands as root on Linux servers with a multipath TCP listener.

As of October 29, Ubuntu and RHEL have not released a fixed kernel. Red Hat, Amazon, Oracle, and SUSE score the flaw between 5.9 and 8.1, lower than the kernel team's 9.8.

The flaw is a race condition in the code that sets up new IPv4 TCP connections. It can make the kernel read memory it has already freed, a bug type known as a use-after-free.

The kernel fix credits Anthropic researcher Xinyang Ge with reporting the bug. Neither the CVE record nor the fix mentions multipath TCP (MPTCP). The link between that feature and this bug comes from Anthropic's post.

MPTCP lets one connection use several network paths at once. On Linux, an application must request MPTCP when it opens a socket.

Anthropic's post says the flaw "was patched upstream and backported to all maintained stable kernel branches." For distribution users, that fix arrives only in the vendor's kernel package. Debian, Oracle Linux, SUSE, and Amazon Linux have shipped fixed packages, at least for some of their kernels, but Ubuntu and RHEL have not.

Ubuntu also lists its cloud, FIPS, and real-time kernels as vulnerable or as work in progress. Red Hat says its fixes are "currently deferred to a future update." Neither Red Hat nor Ubuntu gives a release date.

The race happens during the TCP handshake. When a connection is completed, the kernel hands the IP options stored with the pending request to the new socket without copying them.

If that socket is destroyed while another CPU is still using the options to answer a resent connection request, the kernel reads freed memory.

IPv6 is not affected by this race because the kernel copies the options for IPv6 connections.

The bug was introduced in Linux 4.4. Kernel developers applied a fix on October 5, ten days before the CVE was published.

The fix makes the kernel wait until other CPUs finish reading the options before it frees them.

The kernel's CVE team added the 9.8 score to the CVE record on October 24, nine days after publishing the CVE.

Its score assumes an attacker who sends a TCP connection request carrying IPv4 Record Route or Timestamp options, then resends the request to try to win the race. The team rated attack complexity low, saying both sides of the race are "attacker-induced."

In that case, the team says, the bug could send nearby kernel memory back to the attacker, corrupt kernel memory, or crash the system.

As of October 28, the National Vulnerability Database (NVD) had not added its own score and showed the kernel team's 9.8. Ubuntu's page also shows that score.

Red Hat's CVE page rates the flaw Moderate, scoring it 5.9 because the race is hard to win. It says the most likely result is a kernel crash, with memory corruption possible in theory, and that "no confidentiality or integrity impact has been demonstrated."

Red Hat's machine-readable advisory file, updated on October 29, lists the impact as Important and scores the flaw 8.1, with high confidentiality and integrity impact. Red Hat's bug tracker changed the issue's severity from medium to high the same day. On that day, the CVE page showed Moderate and 5.9.

Oracle and SUSE also score the flaw 8.1, with the same CVSS vector as Red Hat's advisory file. Those scores match the kernel team's on every metric except attack complexity, which the vendors rate high and the kernel team rates low. Amazon scores it 7.0.

CVE 기록과 수정 내용에는 MPTCP 언급이 없으며, 둘을 잇는 내용은 Anthropic의 게시글에만 있다. MPTCP는 하나의 연결이 여러 네트워크 경로를 동시에 쓰게 하며, 리눅스에서는 애플리케이션이 소켓을 열 때 이를 요청해야 한다. 원문은 상류(upstream)에 패치되었고 유지보수 중인 모든 안정 버전에 백포트되었다고 한다. items.title: Herdr has released native app
items.content:
Herdr is a desktop app for terminals and coding agents. Keep work in spaces, see which agents need you, and leave terminals running when you close the window.

curl -fsSL https://releases.herdr.dev/app/install.sh | sh

Linux needs a desktop session and a working Vulkan driver. macOS builds are available for Apple Silicon; Intel Mac users can build from source . Linux builds are x86-64 and ARM64.

The installer adds Herdr to your apps and puts the command in ~/.local/bin .

Add that folder to your PATH if the installer asks.

On macOS the app lives in ~/Applications/Herdr.app .

For drag-and-drop installation on Apple Silicon, download Herdr.dmg and drag Herdr to Applications.

Run in PowerShell on x64 Windows with curl and tar installed (Windows 10 1803 or newer):

irm https: // releases.herdr.dev / app / install.ps1 | iex

Herdr appears in the Start menu. The installer adds %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\herdr-app to your user PATH. Open a new terminal to pick it up.

Both installers download and run code. Read the shell installer or PowerShell installer first if you prefer.

They also install herdr-core if it is missing.

The app can help install or update a core it cannot use.

A space holds work on one machine, usually in one repo. Each space has tabs . Split a tab into panes to put terminals or mod panels beside each other.

An unnamed space follows its first terminal's folder. Name a space or tab when you want a label that stays.

New tabs start in the focused terminal's folder.

The agents sidebar brings agents from your spaces into one list, including workers started by another agent.

Done: finished while you were looking elsewhere.

Idle: not working, or a finished agent you have looked at.

Click an agent to see it. A worker without a pane opens in peek , over your tab. Keep it as a tab if you want it beside your other work.

Ctrl-click a live terminal address in terminal text to peek at it; use Cmd-click on macOS.

An address such as t7 means a terminal on the same machine as the terminal showing it. vps/t7 names one on another machine.

The window arranges terminals. The core runs them.

Closing the window leaves them running; closing a pane or tab ends its terminals.

After a reboot or core crash, kept panes get fresh shells in their last folders, not their old programs.

Add an SSH machine from Settings → Machines or the sidebar's Add machine action.

Pick a host from your SSH config or type how SSH reaches it.

Spaces on that machine run their terminals there, not on your computer.

Each machine keeps its spaces, tabs and splits in its core. Connected screens share that structure and the live terminals, but keep their own focus and zoom.

Remote work keeps running when your local window closes or your laptop sleeps, as long as the remote machine and core stay up.

Open the command palette to find an action by name, or open Settings to change fonts, colors, sounds and other preferences.

The built-in layouts include Herdr, Terminals and Herdr 98.

A layout arranges the window. Mods are small JavaScript programs that draw its panels, menus and dialogs.

Duplicate a shipped layout or mod before changing its structure or code. Your copies stay yours; Herdr updates the shipped ones on start.

Save a personal layout, mod or key file and the window reloads it.

A broken edit keeps the last good version and reports the error.

Ctrl+Shift+P shows every command and its key (Cmd+Shift+P on macOS). Change any key in keys.json ; see the keys section of the mod guide for the format.

Installed releases check for updates in the background and download a new app beside the running one. It takes over when you quit and reopen, or choose the update action. Your terminals keep running in the core.

Settings → Updates shows what is available. What's New opens after an update; you can open it again from the command palette.

Builds from source do not update themselves.

Usage telemetry is on by default in releases. Turn it off in Settings…

Windows 10 1803 이상의 x64에서는 PowerShell 명령으로 설치하며, 시작 메뉴에 등록되고 %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\herdr-app이 사용자 PATH에 추가된다. 두 설치 프로그램 모두 코드를 내려받아 실행하므로 먼저 스크립트를 읽어 보는 것이 좋다. herdr-core가 없으면 함께 설치하며, 앱이 사용할 수 없는 core는 설치 또는 업데이트를 도울 수 있다.

items.title: Miasma Worm Targets AI Coding Agents: 73 Microsoft Azure Repos Disabled
items.content:
An unprecedented supply chain attack bypasses registry-level scanners entirely, turning developer tools including Claude Code, Cursor, and Gemini CLI into execution vectors.

The Incident: On June 3, 2026, a highly sophisticated variant of the Miasma worm (also known as Mini Shai-Hulud) launched a coordinated, two-pronged attack targeting both the npm registry and developer source code repositories.

The Escalation: The attack successfully breached multiple high-profile GitHub accounts, including the official Microsoft Azure durabletask repository, using stolen Personal Access Tokens (PATs) and backdated commits to evade traditional audit trails.

The Response: In an ultra-rapid defensive maneuver, GitHub’s automated mitigation systems disabled 73 compromised repositories – including 49 directly associated with Microsoft, Azure, and Azure-Samples within a mere 105-second window .

The Vector: Instead of relying on traditional package installation hooks, Miasma targets the developer’s local environment. It abuses legitimate auto-run, hook, and rule engines within modern IDEs and AI coding assistants ( VS Code, Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI ) to execute a malicious 4.3 MB staged dropper upon folder-open or agent initialization.

The Impact: Once detonated, the Bun-based worm harvests credentials for AWS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes, npm, and GitHub, and automatically propagates by committing itself back into any repository the victim’s stolen tokens can write to.

At exactly 16:00 UTC on June 3, 2026, a silent, automated purge swept across GitHub. In a high-speed containment action lasting just 105 seconds, 73 active repositories vanished from the platform. Among them were 49 critical repositories belonging to Microsoft, Azure, and Azure-Samples.

This drastic mitigation followed alarming telemetry indicating that threat actors behind the Miasma malware family had regained write access to key cloud repositories. The compromise exploited a stolen Personal Access Token (PAT) belonging to an active Microsoft contributor.

While security firms like StepSecurity and JFrog scrambled to document an concurrent attack vector on the npm registry where 57 malicious packages were published, a second, far more insidious arm of the campaign was already silently spreading directly inside GitHub source repositories.

By bypassing registries and package managers entirely, the Miasma worm targeted the very tools developers use to write code. It didn’t wait for npm install . Instead, it waited for the developer to simply open their code editor or launch an AI coding assistant.

The genius of the Miasma repository-poisoning campaign lies in its exploit surface. When an attacker successfully pushed malicious commits to targeted codebases (such as the popular library icflorescu/mantine-datatable ), the commits added no actual code dependencies.

Instead, the attacker checked in five innocent-looking workspace configuration files and one obfuscated JavaScript file: .github/setup.js .

│ └── settings . json < - - Claude Code SessionStart Hook

│ └── setup . mdc < - - Cursor Agent Prompt Injection

│ └── settings . json < - - Gemini CLI SessionStart Hook

│ └── tasks . json < - - VS Code Automatic Folder - Open Task

├── package . json < -- Hijacked NPM Test Script

└── setup . js < - - The 4.3 MB Staged Dropper

Each of these configuration files is designed to abuse a legitimate, developer-friendly auto-run feature within popular modern tools. Opening the cloned directory in any of these environments instantly triggers execution.

Claude Code & Gemini CLI (SessionStart Hooks)

Both Anthropic’s Claude Code and Google’s Gemini CLI support custom hooks triggered when an AI agent initializes a session in a project workspace. Miasma exploits this by defining a blanket wildcard matcher that forces the agent to execute the dropper via Node.js before any developer prompt is processed.

items.content:
온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.
